To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the EBNA-1/oriP functions differentially contribute to transfection/expression efficiency in mammalian cells.

the EBNA-1/oriP functions differentially contributed to the efficacy of genetic delivery and subsequent expression, which was predominantly attributed to the cytoplasm-to nuclear translocation as well as enhancement in gene expression, but the EBV episomal replication was dispensable for the EBNA- 1/oriP-enhanced transfection/expression in mammalian cells.

the EBNA-1/oriP mediated acceleration of genetic delivery is predominantly due to the enhancement of transcription and cytoplasm-to nuclear recruitment, while the episome replication is not essentially involved.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a nonviral vector with the ability to efficiently deliver and express the exogenous DNA, which is a key step toward the clinical application of gene therapy.
the elucidation of the mechanism of the EBNA-1/oriP-dependent enhancement of genetic delivery and transcription in mammalian cells.
the development of a novel nonviral gene therapy system that is based on the EBV-oriP/EBNA1-mediated acceleration of genetic transfection/expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EBNA-1/oriP functions differentially and cooperatively contribute to the efficacy of genetic delivery and subsequent expression of the plasmid DNA in mammalian cells.

the EBNA-1/oriP is a powerful genetic delivery and expression tool, and the acceleration of genetic delivery is due to the enhancement of cytoplasmic recruitment and nuclear retention of DNA and the acceleration of expression is due to the transcriptional up-regulatory effect of EBNA-1.

the EBNA-1 and oriP are able to promote the transfection and expression of exogenous genes in mammalian cells, which is predominantly due to the enhancement of cytoplasm-nuclear transport as well as transcriptional up-regulatory activities, while the episome replication is not essential for the transfection and transcriptional up-regulations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the EBNA-1/oriP sequence is a potent enhancer of the transfection and expression of plasmid vectors in a broad range of mammalian cells, and the enhancement of the transfection/expression is mainly due to its cytoplasm-to- nuclear transport activity and transcriptional up-regulating function.
the EBNA-1/oriP can be used for the enhancement of transfection/exogenous expression of plasmid DNA in a broad range of mammalian cells.
the EBNA-1/oriP can serve as a powerful tool in gene delivery and expression in various mammalian cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EBNA-1/oriP sequence is an effective and convenient tool for enhancing the efficiency of nonviral gene delivery and expression.
the EBNA-1/oriP can serve as an effective tool for the improvement of genetic delivery and subsequent expression in mammalian systems, especially for the delivery of DNA into the nucleus.

the EBNA-1/oriP can be used as a novel tool for enhancing transfection/expression efficiency of exogenous genes, and that the cytoplasmic retention and nuclear retention functions of the EBNA-ORF1/ORiP are more critical for enhancing transfection efficiency than the replication of the EBNA/ORiP.
